title: PACER: Process-Aware VLA Policy Learning from Human Corrections for Robotic Disassembly
summary: Robotic disassembly of end-of-life (EoL) products requires robots to accommodate product variation, follow prerequisite sequences, and approach components precisely for contact-rich manipulation. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) provides a practical path for adaptation, but limited and costly disassembly data cannot capture the distribution shifts arising from changing environments and product uncertainties. The policy's own rollouts record its approach attempts, and human corrections demonstrate recovery from its errors, but turning these experiences into better policy performance remains challenging. We introduce PACER, a Process-Aware Correction and Evidence Reweighting framework that learns from these experiences through SFT, using progress toward the target and each trace's source and outcome to weight valid action chunks in the native supervised action loss. PACER trains one policy per weighting setting and selects one of the resulting policies through held-out validation. We evaluate PACER on UR5e motherboard disassembly across five component classes, where it achieves 87/100 successful approach-and-handoff trials on the held-out benchmark, compared with 54/100 for vanilla post-SFT.
full_text: Robotic disassembly of end-of-life (EoL) products requires robots to accommodate product variation, follow prerequisite sequences, and approach components precisely for contact-rich manipulation. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) provides a practical path for adaptation, but limited and costly disassembly data cannot capture the distribution shifts arising from changing environments and product uncertainties. The policy's own rollouts record its approach attempts, and human corrections demonstrate recovery from its errors, but turning these experiences into better policy performance remains challenging. We introduce PACER, a Process-Aware Correction and Evidence Reweighting framework that learns from these experiences through SFT, using progress toward the target and each trace's source and outcome to weight valid action chunks in the native supervised action loss. PACER trains one policy per weighting setting and selects one of the resulting policies through held-out validation. We evaluate PACER on UR5e motherboard disassembly across five component classes, where it achieves 87/100 successful approach-and-handoff trials on the held-out benchmark, compared with 54/100 for vanilla post-SFT. Introduction --- Albert Einstein Electronic waste (e-waste) is among the fastest-growing end-of-life (EoL) streams worldwide, but current improper recovery processes impose substantial environmental burdens and leave considerable material value unrealized liu2027transforming, balde2024global . Disassembly is central to recycling and remanufacturing EoL products, but it remains largely manual because workers can adapt to variations in product type and condition. However, manual disassembly is labor-intensive and hard to scale liu2026raise . Robotic automation offers an alternative, but most existing disassembly systems are engineered for known products, with labeled parts, fixed operation sequences, and hand-designed perception and motion modules. Such systems can execute a predefined procedure, but their capability to learn from disassembly experience is limited. The rise of vision-language-action (VLA) models offers a promising direction for enabling robots to learn from operational data end-to-end kim2024openvla, team2024octo, fan2025long . In the disassembly setting, they are used to identify actionable components in complex environments as tasks, plan motions to approach them, and execute precision contact-rich manipulations. However, these tasks differ from the daily-life tabletop tasks on which most current state-of-the-art VLA models are trained. Adapting VLA models to industrial disassembly requires domain post-training. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is the most direct approach, but its effectiveness is limited by the scarcity and narrow coverage of real disassembly demonstrations li2025transferring, liu2025vision . While several agentic systems use VLAs primarily as planners or motion proposers rather than full executors to reduce complexity during contact-rich manipulation liu2026self, guo2026papo , these models still suffer from distribution shift. A policy trained on nominal demonstrations can reach unfamiliar states through its own decisions during deployment. Autonomous rollouts record successful approaches, partial progress, and the states reached during failed attempts. Human corrections collected during rollouts provide recovery actions from policy-induced failure states that clean trajectories may not cover. However, the value of robots' own rollout data and human corrections is obscured when they are simply added to fine-tuning datasets. Clean demonstrations, expert recoveries, autonomous successes, near misses, and failed rollouts differ in reliability and in how they should influence the policy update for better performance. A binary success-or-failure label is also too coarse to explain which parts of a rollout were useful, while asking humans to annotate every step in real-world rollouts is costly. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a formal mechanism for credit assignment from trial experience to drive improvement, and recent work uses it to seek gains beyond SFT baselines in VLA post-training li2025simplevla, chen2025pi_ . However, direct RL in industrial disassembly is costly because contact-induced physical changes are difficult to simulate accurately and efficiently, and learning on real hardware is slow, costly, and safety-sensitive li2025controlvla . Online RL obtains feedback through continued interaction, whereas offline RL learns from existing records using reward signals, value estimates, or advantage estimates zhang2026balancing, levine2020offline, peng2019advantage . Additionally, both RL routes require task-relevant reward specification and may involve adapting the optimization method to the VLA action head chen2025pi_ . We therefore investigate whether SFT can learn more from autonomous experience and human corrections through a unified framework that retains the model's native supervised action loss. We introduce PACER, a process-aware correction and evidence reweighting framework for VLA post-training in robotic disassembly, as shown in Figure~ fig:Intro . PACER learns from autonomous rollouts, human corrections, and supplementary clean demonstrations. It assesses progress toward the intended target within each trace and uses the trace's role to judge which recorded actions provide useful supervision. These assessments translate into bounded weights that scale each valid action chunk's contribution to the native supervised action loss. Different weighting settings specify how process evidence and trace roles are combined to determine these weights. PACER fine-tunes the same reference policy under each setting and selects one of the resulting policies through offline validation. We evaluate the selected policy on real UR5e motherboard disassembly across five component classes. PACER achieves 87/100 successful approach-and-handoff trials on the held-out benchmark, compared with 79/100 for fixed-geometry reweighting and 54/100 for vanilla post-SFT. Related Work Vision-language-action models. Vision-language-action (VLA) models reason over multimodal inputs, including task instructions, enabling the system to use the visual state, understand language prompts, and generate executable actions for robot control in a single model sapkota2025vision, kawaharazuka2025vision, din2025vision . Systems such as RT-2 brohan2023rt , Octo team2024octo , OpenVLA kim2024openvla , OpenVLA-oft kim2025fine , intelligence2025pi_ , and intelligence2026pi show that visual robot policies can transfer across tasks, embodiments, and instructions when trained on large robot datasets. DROID khazatsky2024droid provides real-world manipulation data, while LIBERO liu2023libero benchmarks knowledge transfer in lifelong robot learning. However, most of these models are trained on and targeted at daily-life tabletop tasks under a general manipulation setting. Industrial practice, like disassembly, introduces a different regime in which the policy must operate amid product variation, limited demonstrations, contact-rich execution, and costly real-world evaluation li2025transferring, zhang2025pure . VLA post-training and learning from human corrections. Post-training is the standard mechanism for adapting a pretrained VLA to a specific deployment domain and enhancing task performance xiang2025parallels . Advantage-weighted regression and AWAC use exponentiated estimated advantages as nonnegative weights on a behavior-cloning loss peng2019advantage, nair2020awac . L2RW updates minibatch example weights through validation-based meta-gradients, whereas Meta-Weight-Net uses validation feedback to learn a loss-to-weight function ren2018learning, shu2019meta . Reinforcement learning (RL) extends this principle from supervised reweighting to interactive credit assignment with rollouts and reward signals li2025simplevla, liu2026can . Recent VLA models employ online policy-gradient post-training under sparse success rewards tan2025interactive, lu2025vla, zhang2025robustvla , and extend this approach to deployment settings in which teleoperated interventions are fused with autonomous rollouts through advantage-conditioning, as exemplified by RECAP in and SOP intelligence2025pi, pan2026sop . For learning from human corrections, HandITL and DexHiL embed low-latency arm-hand intervention and prioritize corrective segments during training han2026dexhil, li2026hand . Action preference optimization converts intervention trajectories into preference pairs or language-grounded latent edits xia2026human . Hi-ORS applies reward-threshold rejection sampling and reward-weighted supervision to accepted rollouts lu2025human , and a VLM-based reflective post-training combines PPO guided by dense rewards from failure analysis with supervised fine-tuning on successful experience li2025reflection . Flow-matching VLA heads do not directly expose tractable action log-likelihoods, complicating likelihood-based policy-gradient updates chen2025pi_ . Existing approaches enable policy optimization through stochastic denoising reformulations chen2025pi_ or perform RL in noise space with a frozen flow-matching decoder lu2026unified . Offline and reward-verified variants can reduce the need for live rollouts but still rely on value estimates or reward supervision zhang2026balancing, chen2025conrft, li2025vla . PACER We introduce PACER, a process-aware correction and evidence-reweighting framework for VLA post-training from heterogeneous disassembly traces, as shown in Figure~ fig:2 . PACER operates on the data side and preserves the action representation, the VLA backbone architecture, and the native per-sample action prediction objective, modifying only the sample-level contribution of each training row to that objective. Adaptation is formulated as a validation-selected reweighting problem over typed rollouts, human corrections, and supplementary clean demonstrations collected after an initial supervised training. Starting from an initial demonstration set , PACER trains a supervised reference policy and uses it to construct a separate post-training dataset . The dataset contains autonomous rollouts, operator-initiated corrections, and supplementary clean demonstrations collected under a fixed coverage protocol. Each action-chunk row is assigned a process role from its provenance and operator outcome label. Eligibility gates determine which rows can provide imitation targets. For eligible rows, process evidence and role multipliers determine their contribution to training. Each candidate weighting setting in a finite predeclared set specifies this mapping to bounded training weights, while the evidence features, process roles, and eligibility gates remain fixed. Adapter learning and weight selection are separated. For each setting, the inner loop initializes a fresh low-rank adaptation (LoRA) adapter from the shared SFT checkpoint and trains it under the corresponding weighted action loss. A fixed analytic validator then scores new action chunks predicted by each fitted policy from logged validation observations. The outer loop selects the evidence-to-weight configuration over by validation score, subject to predefined validity and safety checks (audits). The selected policy is then evaluated on held-out hardware tasks. Algorithm~ alg:pacer summarizes the procedure. Data collection. An initial supervised reference policy is fitted on the demonstration set . The reference policy is then deployed as an action-chunk planner across the deployment scenes while the downstream execution stack is kept fixed. Following the agentic VLA framework of SELF-VLA liu2026self , we treat a rollout as successful when the policy reaches a region from which the downstream skill can be executed reliably. After each rollout, the operator assigns one of five labels distinguishing success, near misses, invalid orientation or location, wrong regions

title: SonoWorld: Towards Interactive Pose-Controllable Ultrasound World Models
summary: Robotic ultrasound can standardize image acquisition and reduce operator workload and variability, but policy learning remains limited by the lack of realistic, controllable simulation environments. While controllable world models have advanced rapidly in natural-image domains, ultrasound world modeling remains challenging because each frame captures only a cross-section of unobserved 3D anatomy, causing small probe motions to induce large appearance changes. Existing approaches rely on robot-tracked poses and latent-space prediction, but do not directly generate the observations required for interactive control. We propose SonoWorld, a causal ultrasound world model that learns video dynamics from unlabeled clinical videos and grounds them to 6-DoF control using a small set of freehand clinical scans tracked with an EM sensor. SonoWorld is trained in three stages: pretraining a latent-action-conditioned video diffusion model on around 6.9 million unlabeled multi-organ ultrasound frames; grounding the learned video dynamics to metric probe poses with a small EM-tracked thyroid dataset; and applying distribution matching distillation to enable causal, long-horizon autoregressive generation with selectively caching eviction tokens at inference time. We evaluate controllability through pose-following fidelity, round-trip consistency, and axis-specific control under synthetic actions on held-out tracked scans, and further validate it with a user study. In model-based action discrimination, SonoWorld correctly ranks the target-directed probe motion over an equal-magnitude opposite motion in up to 74.8% of trials. To our knowledge, SonoWorld is the first causal, pose-controllable ultrasound world model learned primarily from freehand clinical videos, providing a data-driven interactive environment for robotic ultrasound data acquisition and policy evaluation.
full_text: Robotic ultrasound can standardize image acquisition and reduce operator workload and variability, but policy learning remains limited by the lack of realistic, controllable simulation environments: physical phantoms and acoustic simulators exhibit a substantial domain gap from clinical images, and trial-and-error exploration on patients is unsafe. While controllable world models have advanced rapidly in natural-image domains, ultrasound world modeling remains challenging because each frame captures only a cross-section of unobserved 3D anatomy, causing small probe motions to induce large appearance changes. Existing approaches rely on robot-tracked poses and latent-space prediction, but do not directly generate the observations required for interactive control. We propose SonoWorld, a causal ultrasound world model that learns video dynamics from unlabeled clinical videos and grounds them to 6-DoF control using a small set of freehand clinical scans tracked with an electromagnetic (EM) sensor. SonoWorld is trained in three stages: pretraining a latent-action-conditioned video diffusion model on around 6.9 million unlabeled multi-organ ultrasound frames; grounding the learned video dynamics to metric probe poses with a small EM-tracked thyroid dataset; and applying distribution matching distillation to enable causal, long-horizon autoregressive generation with selectively caching eviction tokens at inference time. We evaluate controllability through pose-following fidelity, round-trip consistency, and axis-specific control under synthetic actions on held-out tracked scans, and further validate it with a user study. In model-based action discrimination, SonoWorld correctly ranks the target-directed probe motion over an equal-magnitude opposite motion in up to 74.8 of trials. To our knowledge, SonoWorld is the first causal, pose-controllable ultrasound world model learned primarily from freehand clinical videos, providing a data-driven interactive environment for robotic ultrasound data acquisition and policy evaluation. Project page is available under . Introduction Ultrasound is among the most widely used diagnostic imaging modalities, valued for its real-time imaging, absence of ionizing radiation, portability, and low cost~ wang2020anatomy,jiang2023robotic . Unlike many imaging modalities, however, ultrasound acquisition is inherently interactive: the observed image depends on the six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) pose of a hand-held probe, which the operator continuously adjusts to navigate anatomy and acquire diagnostically standard views. Consequently, image quality and diagnostic yield depend heavily on operator expertise, contributing to substantial inter-operator variability and a persistent shortage of trained sonographers~ jiang2023robotic . Robotic ultrasound offers a promising path toward standardized image acquisition, reduced operator workload, and broader access to expert-level scanning, particularly in remote and resource-limited settings~ du2024robot . Realizing this potential requires robotic scanning policies that map observed ultrasound images to probe motions, whose development and evaluation in turn require realistic interactive environments in which the visual consequences of probe actions can be observed. Existing environments for robotic ultrasound expose a fundamental trade-off between controllability, realism, and safety. Physical phantoms and physics-based simulators permit controlled exploration over probe poses, but their synthetic anatomy and image formation leave a substantial domain gap from clinical ultrasound~ shams2008realtime, burger2013realtime, gao2009fast . Re-slicing reconstructed 3D ultrasound volumes provides more realistic observations, but requires subject-specific tracked acquisitions and cannot faithfully reproduce view-dependent appearance changes under arbitrary probe orientations~ lasso2014plus . Scanning real patients provides observations from the true clinical distribution, yet repeated trial-and-error exploration is neither practical nor safe. An alternative line of work bypasses explicit simulation and learns probe guidance or autonomous scanning directly from tracked clinical scans and expert demonstrations~ jiang2024cardiaccopilot,jiang2024structure,yue2025echoworld,su2024fully,jiang2025towards . While effective, this paradigm depends on collecting real image--action trajectories at scale and does not provide a reusable environment for evaluating counterfactual probe actions before they are executed on patients. These limitations motivate a controllable generative environment learned directly from clinical ultrasound videos, capable of synthesizing realistic future observations in response to probe actions without tracking each patient. Controllable world models offer a promising data-driven alternative by learning to predict future observations conditioned on actions, and have emerged as powerful interactive simulators for games, autonomous driving, and robotic manipulation~ hou2026world,ding2025understanding,gao2026dreamdojo . Ultrasound, however, presents a distinct challenge: each frame captures only a 2D cross-section of unobserved 3D anatomy, such that small probe motions, particularly out-of-plane translations and rotations, can induce large changes in image appearance. Existing ultrasound world models address this challenge using robot-tracked acquisitions~ fan2026action and latent-space prediction~ yue2025echoworld, jiang2024cardiaccopilot , but do not directly generate future ultrasound observations from freehand 6-DoF probe actions. Consequently, a causal, pose-controllable world model that can generate realistic ultrasound observations directly from clinical data remains largely unexplored. We introduce SonoWorld, a causal, pose-controllable ultrasound world model that learns ultrasound video dynamics primarily from large-scale unlabeled clinical videos and requires only a small set of EM-tracked scans to acquire 6-DoF control. Inspired by previous works~ gao2025adaworld,gao2026dreamdojo , SonoWorld is trained in three stages: First, we pretrain a latent-action video diffusion model on around 6.9 million unlabeled multi-organ ultrasound frames, allowing it to capture both probe-induced appearance changes and physiological dynamics without pose annotations. Second, we ground the learned dynamics to physical probe motion by post-training on a small set of calibrated EM-tracked thyroid scans, where probe motion is represented as relative 6-DoF actions in the probe coordinate frame. Finally, we distill the bidirectional model into a causal autoregressive generator using self-forcing and selectively retain informative KV-cache tokens, enabling stable long-horizon interactive rollouts. Our main contributions are summarized as follows: We introduce SonoWorld, to our knowledge the first causal, interactive, pose-controllable ultrasound world model that directly generates future ultrasound observations conditioned on 6-DoF probe actions, providing an interactive learned environment for robotic ultrasound data acquisition and policy evaluation. We develop a scalable training strategy that learns ultrasound dynamics from around 6.9 million unlabeled multi-organ clinical frames and grounds them to probe control using only a small set of EM-tracked scans. This enables large-scale dynamics learning without pose annotations, while requiring costly tracker-acquired data only for the subsequent physical action-grounding stage. We convert the bidirectional video model into a causal autoregressive generator through self-forcing and introduce selective KV-cache retention for streaming inference, enabling extended action-conditioned rollouts while preserving generation quality. We evaluate SonoWorld under measured, accelerated, round-trip, and axis-specific synthetic probe motions, and further conduct a user study with experienced ultrasound raters assessing image quality, video consistency, and probe--anatomy alignment. Related Work Generative World Models sec:rw_world_models Generative world models learn action-conditioned dynamics of visual environments and have emerged as a scalable paradigm for interactive simulation across embodied AI~ nvidia2025cosmos,yang2024unisim,jang2025dreamgen,gao2026dreamdojo,huang2026vid2world , games~ bruce2024genie,alonso2024diamond,kanervisto2025wham , autonomous driving~ hu2023gaia,gao2024vista,yang2025resim . A central challenge in scaling such models is that action-labeled data are far less abundant than passive video. Latent-action models address this imbalance by discovering control-relevant dynamics directly from visual observations: Genie~ bruce2024genie learns discrete latent actions, AdaWorld~ gao2025adaworld extends them to a continuous action space, and subsequent work like DreamDojo scales this paradigm to real-world robotic application~ gao2026dreamdojo and grounds learned latent actions into executable robot commands~ ye2025lapa . This separation between learning visual dynamics from abundant unlabeled video and grounding them to physical actions provides a natural foundation for domains where paired action--video data are costly to acquire. Medical World Models In the medical field generative world models have recently emerged as learned simulators for medical video. Endora~ li2024endora models spatiotemporal dynamics to generate realistic endoscopic videos, while Surgical Vision World Model~ koju2025surgicalvision learns latent actions from unlabeled surgical videos for controllable generation, and SAW~ rapuri2026saw further conditions laparoscopic video generation on language, tissue affordances, and 2D tool trajectories. In ultrasound, Cardiac Copilot~ jiang2024cardiaccopilot learns a latent spatial model from tracked echocardiography and predicts structural features of neighboring cardiac planes for probe guidance; Structure-aware World Model~ jiang2024structure extends this paradigm with large-scale self-supervised learning of anatomical representations under 3D pose transformations; and EchoWorld~ yue2025echoworld incorporates motion-induced visual dynamics and visual--motion history for sequential probe guidance, but these methods use world modeling primarily for representation learning rather than as image-generating interactive environments. More recently, Fan et al.~ fan2026action predict future ultrasound observations conditioned on tracked probe motions and use the learned dynamics for goal-plane navigation. In contrast, SonoWorld learns ultrasound dynamics primarily from large-scale untracked clinical videos, grounds them to metric 6-DoF probe actions using a small tracked subset, and causally generates future observations under these actions, enabling interactive rollouts for policy evaluation and model-based action discrimination. Interactive Ultrasound Environments sec:rw_environments Several strategies exist for building an environment in which probe motion can be explored. Physical phantoms provide genuine acoustic interaction but lack clinical appearance and encode a single fixed anatomy. Physics-based simulation renders images from a CT-derived anatomical model at arbitrary poses~ shams2008realtime, burger2013realtime, salehi2015patient , yet ray-casting cannot reproduce speckle from first principles~ gao2009fast and wave-accurate solvers are too slow to be interactive~ jaros2016full . General-purpose robotics platforms such as NVIDIA Isaac Sim support scalable robotic ultrasound simulation and policy training, but their simplified ultrasound image formation does not faithfully capture the acoustic properties of clinical ultrasound~ gao2026nvidia . Sim-to-real translation narrows the appearance gap~ vitale2020improving at the cost of physical consistency. Freehand reconstruction compounds a tracked sweep into a volume that can be re-sliced~ lasso2014plus , but view-dependent effects are frozen at the acquisition angle and every simulated subject needs its own

title: Paraphrase Consensus Is Not Self-Consistency: Instruction Reliance and Robustness in VLA Policies
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies fine-tuned on LIBERO are trained and evaluated on the same ten instruction strings, and rewording the instruction changes base OpenVLA's success by -38.0 points. Test-time prompt ensembling, which improves language models, does not recover this loss in any setting we ran. Paraphrase consensus (the medoid action over K paraphrases) costs base OpenVLA 16.8 points when the training instruction is a member. Without it, the medoid of the paraphrases scores -32.4 points relative to the training instruction, and confidence-based selection scores -28.0. The same medoid over samples of one paraphrase improves on greedy decoding but stays -27.6 points below the training instruction, consistent with aggregation reducing variance without removing the bias the paraphrases share. A wrong-instruction probe measures how much of a policy's success depends on the instruction. Across three policies and four suites, paraphrases cost a policy only where this share is high, and the stronger policies lose a much smaller fraction of it than base OpenVLA. LoRA post-training on paraphrased instructions reduces the one-paraphrase effect to +2.0 points, against -32.0 for a matched control, reproduces across two seeds and on OpenVLA-OFT, transfers to withheld phrasings, and leaves the policy's reliance on the instruction unchanged.

Test-time prompt ensembling, which improves language models, does not recover this loss in any setting we ran. Paraphrase consensus (the medoid action over paraphrases) costs base OpenVLA points when the training instruction is a member. The same medoid over samples of one paraphrase improves on greedy decoding but stays points below the training instruction, consistent with aggregation reducing variance without removing the bias the paraphrases share. Across three policies and four suites, paraphrases cost a policy only where this share is high, and the stronger policies lose a much smaller fraction of it than base OpenVLA. LoRA post-training on paraphrased instructions reduces the one-paraphrase effect to points, against for a matched control, reproduces across two seeds and on OpenVLA-OFT, transfers to withheld phrasings, and leaves the policy's reliance on the instruction unchanged. Introduction sec:intro Vision-language-action (VLA) policies map a camera image and a natural-language instruction to robot actions~ brohan2023rt1,zitkovich2023rt2,kim2024openvla,black2024pi0 . Many are language models fine-tuned to emit actions. OpenVLA~ kim2024openvla , for example, is a 7B Llama-2 model that outputs actions as vocabulary tokens. On LIBERO~ liu2023libero , the standard simulation benchmark for these policies, each released checkpoint is fine-tuned on exactly ten instructions, one fixed string per task, and evaluated on the same ten strings, character for character~ kim2025oft , which in NLP terms is an extreme case of single-template instruction tuning. Users will not phrase a request exactly as the training data did, and language models are sensitive to how a prompt is worded~ sclar2024quantifying,lu2022fantastically,sun2024evaluating,mizrahi2024state , so a benchmark score says little about what happens when the instruction is reworded. We ask how much rewording costs such a policy, and whether that loss can be recovered at test time, without retraining, the way prompt ensembling and self-consistency recover accuracy for language models. The natural test-time remedy comes from language models. Self-consistency~ wang2023selfconsistency samples several answers and keeps the majority, and prompt ensembling~ jiang2020know aggregates answers over rewordings of a query. The VLA analogue is paraphrase consensus: rephrase the instruction ways, query the policy once per phrasing, and execute the medoid, the action closest to all the others, a continuous majority vote that always returns one of the policy's own actions. It needs no training or verifier, and test-time selection over sampled actions already helps VLAs~ kwok2025robomonkey,jang2026mgselect . Prompt ensembling, however, works for language models pre-trained on many phrasings, where rewordings are comparably good prompts. A VLA fine-tuned on one string per task has seen only one good prompt, and every paraphrase may be a worse one. We implement paraphrase consensus ( , ) with paired, per-step logging and run it on OpenVLA-OFT (LIBERO-Spatial with and without a distractor object, and Goal) and base OpenVLA (Spatial and Long). For these two policies and on all four suites, we also measure how much of each policy's success needs the instruction at all. We find that unweighted consensus does not help. The per-step logs trace the failure to the members themselves, which points to a fix at training time. Test-time consensus does not recover what a paraphrase costs. One paraphrase, held for the episode, changes base OpenVLA's success by points. Consensus with the training instruction among the members costs base OpenVLA points and OFT on Goal; without it, neither the medoid of the paraphrases nor the paraphrase the policy is most confident in comes close to the training instruction ( , ). The reason is that paraphrases are not exchangeable. Self-consistency aggregates draws from one conditional, whereas paraphrases are conditionals, only one of which the policy was fit to. The same medoid over samples of one paraphrase does reduce variance, beating greedy decoding by , yet stays below the training instruction ( sec:weak ). A paraphrase costs a policy only where its success needs the instruction. A wrong-instruction probe, a partial-input baseline~ poliak2018hypothesis,gururangan2018annotation,kaushik2018much,thomason2019shifting , gives another task's instruction in the same scene. Base OpenVLA needs the instruction for nearly all of its success on every suite. OpenVLA-OFT and ~ intelligence2025pi05 pay a paraphrase cost only on LIBERO-Goal, where all of their success needs the instruction, and lose a far smaller fraction of it than base OpenVLA does ( sec:probe ). This qualifies LIBERO-Plus's conclusion that fine-tuned VLAs ``degenerate into vision-action models''~ fei2025liberoplus . The fix is at training time. LoRA post-training on the same demonstrations with paraphrased instructions moves the one-paraphrase effect from to , while a matched control trained on the original instructions stays at . The result holds for a second seed, transfers to phrasings withheld from training, carries to OpenVLA-OFT on Goal, and leaves the policy reading its instruction. It costs about an hour of training once, whereas consensus queries four instructions at every step ( sec:aug ). Contributions. (i)~A paired, per-timestep measurement of paraphrase consensus on two policies in five settings, with the mechanism read from the logs and tested by an exchangeable-sampling control and a confidence-weighted selector. (ii)~An instruction-reliance probe on all LIBERO suites, a partial-input baseline for embodied models, and the finding that paraphrase cost appears only where reliance is high, across twelve policy--suite pairs from three policies. (iii)~The established remedy, training on paraphrases~ xiao2022dial , measured with three controls we did not find reported for prior remedies~ hou2026langgap,yin2026gsr : a matched training control, transfer to withheld phrasings and types, and a grounding check. Related Work sec:related VLAs and their language robustness. Large pretrained policies map images and language to actions~ brohan2023rt1,zitkovich2023rt2,ghosh2024octo,kim2024openvla,black2024pi0,intelligence2025pi05 . OpenVLA-OFT adds parallel decoding, a continuous action head and chunking~ kim2025oft . LIBERO's perturbation suites reach opposite conclusions on language: LIBERO-Plus finds fine-tuned VLAs largely ignore the instruction~ fei2025liberoplus , LIBERO-PRO reports collapse under minimal rewording~ zhou2025liberopro , and LIBERO-Para quantifies the collapse at -- points under paraphrase across seven VLAs, attributed to surface-level matching rather than semantic grounding~ kim2026liberopara . xing2025shortcut attribute language-ignoring to shortcut learning, and LangGap shows largely ignores instructions when one task per layout lets it~ hou2026langgap . LIBERO-Para is built on LIBERO-Goal, where its paraphrases cost OFT about points. Ours cost it there and base OpenVLA . Our generator preserves every object reference, and LIBERO-Para attributes most of its drop to object-level lexical variation. What these diagnostics do not ask is whether test-time aggregation recovers the loss, or how the penalty relates to how much of a score needs the instruction at all ( sec:probe ). Perturbation ensembles and failure detection. Ensemble disagreement~ lakshminarayanan2017ensembles,ovadia2019trust,menda2019ensembledagger,hoque2021thriftydagger,romer2025fiper,lee2026pfd,shanmugam2021tta and runtime monitors~ agia2024stac,gu2025safe,seligmann2026vlafail,karli2025askbefore are compared with paraphrase on identical trajectories in App.~ sec:sensitivity and app:failure . Prompt sensitivity, self-consistency and test-time scaling. LLMs are sensitive to how a prompt is worded: formatting~ sclar2024quantifying , example order~ lu2022fantastically and paraphrased instructions~ sun2024evaluating,mizrahi2024state move accuracy by many points. Prompt ensembling~ jiang2020know , self-consistency~ wang2023selfconsistency , semantic entropy~ kuhn2023semantic,farquhar2024semantic and paraphrase-based uncertainty~ gao2024spuq,khan2024consistency aggregate over samples or prompts in discrete output spaces. The medoid is minimum-Bayes-risk selection, of which self-consistency is a special case~ bertsch2023mbr , and MBR over several prompts' outputs helps text generation~ heineman2024mbr . For VLAs, RoboMonkey scores sampled actions with a verifier~ kwok2025robomonkey and MG-Select scores against a condition-masked reference~ jang2026mgselect , and both sample the action axis from one prompt. Paraphrase consensus samples the instruction axis. Aggregators built for prompts of unequal quality weight members by held-out accuracy~ jiang2020know,arora2023ask or zero-shot scores~ allingham2023zeroshot , and lower-perplexity prompts work better~ gonen2023demystifying . With one member known to be the training instruction, that weighting degenerates to selecting it, which is the canonical controller. sec:weak shows the difference between the two axes is decisive. Remedies. Training on more phrasings is an established remedy. DIAL relabels demonstrations with VLM-generated instructions to broaden what a policy can follow~ xiao2022dial , SPRINT relabels for pre-training~ zhang2023sprint , and RT-1 trained on diverse phrasings~ brohan2023rt1 . LangGap closes its language gap with targeted training-time augmentation~ hou2026langgap , and GSR argues the brittleness is architectural and retrains an action expert on separately extracted task semantics~ yin2026gsr . In NLP, multi-template instruction tuning~ wei2022finetuned,sanh2022multitask , consistency training under back-translation paraphrases~ xie2020unsupervised , and prompt- and paraphrase-consistency objectives~ zhou2022prompt,elazar2021measuring,sun2024evaluating are the precedents for training on rewordings, and our paraphrase types are CheckList-style invariance tests~ ribeiro2020beyond for an embodied model. sec:aug adds three measurements we did not find in these works: a matched training control that separates the phrasings from the extra steps, transfer to withheld phrasings, and a check that the remedy does not work by ignoring the instruction. Paraphrase Consensus sec:method Setting. At replanning step a frozen policy maps observation and instruction to an action chunk ; receding-horizon control executes steps and re-queries. We are given with the training instruction (the benchmark's canonical string) and semantically equivalent paraphrases. Including makes this the most favourable test of test-time computation over phrasings, and sec:weak also runs the deployable ensemble without it. is not modified, and only what is queried and what is executed changes. Paraphrase sets. sec:paraphrase For each task an LLM generates candidates instructed to preserve every object, attribute, spatial relation and goal while varying lexical choice and syntax. Candidates are kept if an independent LLM judge rates them equivalent and their sentence-embedding cosine to the training instruction exceeds a threshold, and the final sets are chosen by greedy max--min selection on embedding distance. Per task we release an llm set, easy (lexical substitution), hard (structural rewrite), adversarial (typos and casing) and a held-out set never used at training time (examples in Tab.~ tab:example ). Prompts, judge, embedding model and threshold are in App.~ app:paraphrases . unless stated. One author, blind to type and suite

title: Active Generative Simulation: Meta-Learning What to Simulate for Sim-and-Real Policy Co-Training
summary: Sim-and-real co-training is an effective way to scale robot learning by augmenting limited real-world demonstrations with simulation data. However, existing approaches typically treat simulators as fixed data sources, relying on uniform generation, offline retrieval, or manual parameter alignment by domain experts. We formulate \textit{Active Generative Simulation}: optimizing a simulator's data-generation distribution to maximize downstream real-world performance. To solve this problem, we propose MetaGenSim, a meta-learning framework that trains an auxiliary rater network via meta-gradients to automatically discover high-utility data-generation distributions within a user-specified simulation parameter space, without manual parameter alignment. Across simulation and real-world manipulation tasks, MetaGenSim outperforms uniform generation and retrieval baselines, achieves a 150% relative improvement in real-world full-task success over uniform generation, and matches expert manual alignment. We further show that distributions curated with a lightweight proxy policy transfer to VLA fine-tuning, and that MetaGenSim can exploit partial alignment through atomic skill stitching and object-receptacle composition when exact sim-and-real task alignment is unavailable. Project website: https://meta-gensim.github.io

Project website: Active Generative Simulation via . Sim-and-real co-training (top) boosts robot performance but traditionally relies on manual alignment (middle), where experts must laboriously tune data generation parameters (such as tasks, object placements, camera poses). We propose (bottom), which meta-learns a Rater to score synthetic data based on policy utility. This induces a utility landscape over parameters, enabling active generation of targeted simulation data that matches the real-world distribution without manually tuning the generation parameters. fig:teaser Introduction While recent large-scale real-robot datasets have advanced generalist policies~ ebert2021bridge, rt12022arxiv, black2026pi0visionlanguageactionflowmodel , relying exclusively on real data remains expensive, labor-intensive, and safety-constrained. Generative simulation offers a scalable alternative data source by procedurally synthesizing scene layouts, assets, and tasks~ Deitke2022ProcTHORLa, liang2024eurekaverse, deshpande2025graspmolmo, katara2024gen2sim, robocasa2024 . We refer to the variables controlling these environments, such as camera poses, object arrangements, visual appearance, and task goals, as data generation parameters. Given data generation parameters, a generative simulator can instantiate environments and generate large numbers of demonstrations with minimal human intervention~ mandlekar2023mimicgen, jiang2024dexmimicgen, garrett2024skillgen, cheng2023nod, lin2026humanoidmimicgendatagenerationlocomanipulation . However, the utility of simulation data remains limited by the sim-to-real gap. Domain randomization and system identification can mitigate this mismatch, but often require substantial human effort and cannot eliminate residual gaps~ jain2025polarisscalablerealtosimevaluations . A promising alternative is sim-and-real co-training, where real demonstrations anchor learning to the deployment domain while simulation provides scale and diversity~ ankile2024imitationrefinementresidual, wei2025simandrealcotraining, maddukuri2025simandreal, cheng2025generalizable, lei2026mechanisticanalysis . Co-training can outperform training on real data alone~ maddukuri2025simandreal, wei2025simandrealcotraining, anonymous2025robocasa , but not all generated data is useful: misaligned camera poses, object layouts, visual factors, or task goals can provide little benefit, and exact alignment may be impossible when the simulator lacks the target setting. This raises a central question: Among the vast space of possible simulation environments, which data should be generated to maximize the performance of a sim-and-real co-trained policy? Current simulation data-generation strategies largely rely on manual heuristics~ mu2024adademo, gao2024efficient or uniform randomization~ torne2024reconciling,tobin2017domain . Overly broad training distributions can degrade policy learning when many samples are irrelevant to the target task~ dass2025datamil,agia2025cupid, kuhar2023learning,chen2025curating,memmel2024strap . Prior work suggests that task-aware alignment helps~ wei2025simandrealcotraining , but manually tuning high-dimensional generation parameters is laborious, requires expert knowledge, and can be misleading when exact alignment is impossible. In this work, we formulate Active Generative Simulation: determining a distribution over simulation parameters such that co-training on the resulting synthetic data maximizes target-task performance. To efficiently tackle this problem, we propose , a meta-learning framework that uses a sparse probing dataset to train an auxiliary rater network, which assigns utility scores to simulation samples based on their contribution to real-world validation performance, automatically guiding the active generation of a targeted synthetic dataset. In summary, our core contributions are: [leftmargin=*, itemsep=0pt, topsep=0pt, parsep=0pt, partopsep=0pt] We formulate Active Generative Simulation, shifting simulation data generation from fixed distribution to controllable and targeted synthesis. We introduce , a meta-learning framework that trains an auxiliary rater network via meta-gradients to discover high-utility data-generation distributions within a user-specified parameter space, without manual parameter alignment. We show that outperforms uniform generation and offline retrieval, achieving a relative improvement in real-world full-task success over uniform generation while matching the performance of manual expert alignment. We demonstrate scalability and generalization of : proxy-curated datasets transfer to fine-tuning , and can exploit partially aligned data when exact task alignment is unavailable. Recent progress in generative modeling~ nvidia2024edify3d, chen2023fantasia3d , motion synthesis~ mandlekar2023mimicgen, cheng2024nodtamp, xue2025demogen , and procedural environment generation~ Deitke2022ProcTHORLa, liang2024eurekaverse has enabled automated simulation pipelines that scale synthetic robot data~ wang2023robogen, katara2024gen2sim, huagensim2, torne2024reconciling, dai2024automated, tian2025interndataa1pioneeringhighfidelitysynthetic, li2025momagen, gong2025anytask, saxena2024cdm . In contrast, leverages a small set of target-task data to actively guide simulation data generation toward high-utility parameter regions. Sim-and-real alignment and policy co-training. title: Robota-Embed: Unified VLA Embeddings for Robot In-Context Learning and Evolution
summary: Retrieving useful context for a robot requires matching its task, execution stage, and the continuation that should follow. We introduce Robota-Embed, to our knowledge the first vision-language-action (VLA) embedding model to jointly encode all three modalities in both current-state queries and recorded future continuations. Predictive retrieval training aligns these endpoints, enabling historical continuations to serve as context at inference time. We construct a multi-source corpus of 1,695,684 cleaned training anchors and introduce Robota-Embed-Bench, with 4,000 queries and a shared 8,000-entry gallery. Robota-Embed achieves 47.33% clip-level and 81.77% episode-level R@1, exceeding action-free Gemini Embedding 2 by 22.09 and 33.47 percentage points. Controlled retrieval studies show that removing native action degrades retrieval more than removing vision. We study two complementary applications. Embed2ICL uses retrieved experience for training-free and training-based policy conditioning, increasing success from 47.0% to 56.3% in DROID-Sim and from 86.4% to 92.8% on the LIBERO difficult subset, while improving task progress on real robots. Embed2Evolve uses execution feedback to grow task-local memory and refine context use around a frozen GPT-6 Astra policy. Across five ManiSkill tasks, it achieves 68% success, compared with 24% for GPT-6 Astra Direct and 33% for a harness independently evolved with Omni-Embed-Nemotron-3B under the same protocol. Relative to the latter, it uses approximately 79.5% fewer policy tokens per test rollout, counting both successes and failures. These results show that a unified, action-aware retrieval space can support robot in-context learning and task-local context evolution.
full_text: Introduction sec:introduction Robot policies increasingly use experience supplied in context. GEN-1.5~ generalist2026gen15 and S1~ skild2026s1 demonstrate Robot In-Context Learning from sensorimotor or video examples. In our experiments, GPT-6 Astra~ openaigpt6astra generates robot actions from observations and execution history. These capabilities make experience selection part of the control problem. Demonstration-conditioned world action models (WAMs) need useful existing examples; policies acting repeatedly must organize accumulated experience. Both raise a representation question: how should physical experience be represented for task- and stage-sensitive retrieval? Task similarity alone is insufficient. Reaching toward a bowl and withdrawing after placement can share objects and an instruction yet require different continuations. Language specifies the goal, vision the interaction state, and native action the ongoing motion. The retrieval endpoints have different temporal roles: the query describes the present, whereas a candidate records what followed an earlier interaction. Predictive retrieval therefore requires sensitivity to task intent and execution stage: the goal is an appropriate recorded continuation, not simply a similar scene. General-purpose embeddings align vision and language~ radford2021learning,girdhar2023imagebind,xu2025omni , while action-aware metric learning connects perception or language with behavior~ sung2017deep,rana2023contrastive . We introduce , a unified vision--language--action (VLA) embedding model for physical-experience retrieval. To our knowledge, it is the first to jointly encode all three modalities in both current-state queries and recorded continuations. Each endpoint yields one vector, so native action informs retrieval itself. Source-specific projectors handle heterogeneous action formats. Retrieval training combines predictive alignment, multimodal grounding and discrimination, and representation regularization. We construct a multi-source training corpus and introduce , with 4,000 queries and 8,000 gallery candidates spanning human, simulated, and real-robot experience. Nearby same-episode clips distinguish finding the right experience from locating its recorded continuation. Across four sources, achieves 47.33 clip-level and 81.77 episode-level R@1. Native action adds information beyond text and images: with backbone, data, and training budget matched on DROID, adding action raises clip-level R@1 from 59.8 to 78.7 . Complementary retraining and query-masking studies examine which information the representation learns and uses. Compared with this baseline, which reaches 33 success, Embed2Evolve uses approximately 79.5 fewer policy tokens per test rollout, including failures. The retrieval representation therefore matters for both memory selection and the final harness's success and token use. We make four contributions. Given a current VLA state, retrieves the video and actions that followed an anchor in a recorded trajectory. For sample from source , the query combines instruction , an interaction-region image , and synchronized native action . The paired target combines the same instruction with a four-second video clip and aligned actions recorded strictly after : Action-Native Predictive VLA Embeddings sec:method-embedding We train for current-to-future retrieval using Cosmos3-Edge 4B~ nvidia2026cosmos3 as the base model (Figure~ fig:pai-embedding-objective ). title: Holi-Spatial 360: Generative Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramas for Spatial Rendering and Intelligence
summary: Spatial intelligence requires scalable 3D environments that are both photorealistic and semantically grounded, yet existing indoor datasets are dominated by room-scale captures and costly LiDAR acquisition. Online real-estate platforms offer abundant panoramas of diverse multi-room homes, but sparse viewpoints and texture-poor regions make reconstruction severely under-constrained. We introduce Holi-Spatial 360, a generative reconstruction and data curation framework for converting these panoramas into annotated multi-room 3D environments. Because reconstruction quality bounds subsequent generation, our Correspondence-Guided Geometric Optimization converts feed-forward reconstruction priors into reliable cross-view constraints and builds a coherent 3D Gaussian Splatting representation as 3D spatial memory. Adapted single-image and video priors then restore appearance and complete continuous trajectories while preserving observed content. The reconstructed scenes support arbitrary RGB-D rendering and an automated curation pipeline that combines end-to-end 3D grounding with VLM-based verification. Holi360 contains over 1K multi-room 3DGS scenes, more than 100K instance annotations, and 2M spatial question-answer pairs. We also introduce the Holi360 benchmark to evaluate the spatial understanding of VLMs in real-world, multi-room indoor environments. Experiments demonstrate superior reconstruction and curation quality under sparse panoramic inputs, while fine-tuning VLMs on Holi360 substantially improves spatial reasoning capabilities.

Online real-estate platforms offer abundant panoramas of diverse multi-room homes, but sparse viewpoints and texture-poor regions make reconstruction severely under-constrained. Adapted single-image and video priors then restore appearance and complete continuous trajectories while preserving observed content. The reconstructed scenes support arbitrary RGB-D rendering and an automated curation pipeline that combines end-to-end 3D grounding with VLM-based verification. Experiments demonstrate superior reconstruction and curation quality under sparse panoramic inputs, while fine-tuning VLMs on Holi360 substantially improves spatial reasoning capabilities. Introduction Spatial intelligence aims to equip large models~ Qwen3-VL,team2023gemini,Qwen2.5-VL with the ability to perceive, ground, reason, and act in the 3D world. Its progress depends on scalable 3D environments that are both photorealistic and semantically grounded. Multi-room homes are particularly important for embodied applications, where understanding must extend beyond individual objects to layouts and relationships across interconnected spaces. However, existing indoor datasets remain difficult to scale. ScanNet~ dai2017scannet and ScanNet++~ yeshwanth2023scannet++ are dominated by room-scale captures, while building-scale datasets such as Matterport3D~ Matterport3D and HM3D~ ramakrishnan2021habitat rely on dedicated capture and processing. SAGE-3D~ miao2026towards provides semantically annotated 3DGS environments but builds upon designed 3D assets and expert annotation. Holi-Spatial~ gao2026holi automates spatial data curation from videos, yet relies on densely captured trajectories with continuous camera motion and sufficient view overlap. Diverse, real-world multi-room environments with both high-quality reconstruction and semantic supervision therefore remain costly to obtain. Online real-estate platforms offer a largely untapped alternative: abundant 360-degree panoramas of diverse multi-room homes. Yet these panoramas are captured at only a few widely separated locations. Limited overlap, texture-poor surfaces, and extensive unobserved regions make cross-view matching and geometric reconstruction unreliable~ ren2025panosplatt3r,jin2026planargs . Recent image- and video-based generative methods can repair artifacts in novel views~ wu2025difix3d+,yin2025gsfixer,de2026artifixer,wang2026artifactworld , but they do not by themselves establish reliable geometry from sparse, multi-room panoramas. When the initial reconstruction is misaligned, generated views may drift from the observed scene and reinforce errors when distilled back into 3D. To address these challenges, we introduce Holi-Spatial 360, a generative reconstruction and data curation framework that transforms sparse panoramas into semantically annotated multi-room 3D environments. Our key insight is that reconstruction quality sets the ceiling for generation. Correspondence-Guided Geometric Optimization uses priors from feed-forward large reconstruction models~ wang2025vggt,lin2025depth to establish cross-view constraints and optimize a coherent initial 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representation. This representation serves as persistent spatial memory for generative trajectory densification: image and video priors restore and complete novel views, which are distilled back into 3D while remaining grounded in the observed panoramas. The scenes support RGB-D rendering and automated spatial data curation, including verified 3D instances, grounding annotations, and spatial question-answer pairs. The pipeline requires only RGB panoramas, without depth capture or human-in-the-loop labeling. From publicly available real-estate and rental panoramas, we construct Holi360: over 1K multi-room 3DGS scenes, dense RGB-D renderings and meshes, more than 100K verified 3D instances, and 2M spatial question-answer pairs. Reconstruction and annotation use only RGB panoramas; RealSee3D~ Li2025realsee3d_data LiDAR and semantic maps are reserved for evaluation. Experiments show improved rendering, geometry, and grounding, while VLM fine-tuning on Holi360 boosts spatial reasoning. related work Scalable Indoor Environments for Spatial Intelligence Recent datasets such as SenseNova-SI-800K~ cai2025scaling and VST-P~ yang2025visual scale spatial supervision, but annotation count does not imply environment diversity. EmbodiedScan~ embodiedscan and SceneSplat-7K~ li2025scenesplat reuse existing scans, while HM3DSEM~ yadav2023habitatmatterport3dsemanticsdataset , HM3D-OVON~ Yokoyama2024HM3DOVONAD , and GOAT-Bench~ Khanna2024GOATBenchAB derive further annotations or tasks from HM3D~ ramakrishnan2021habitat . These efforts enrich supervision over a largely fixed pool of 3D assets. We instead scale the pool itself by reconstructing diverse, real-world multi-room homes from online panoramas. Generative Reconstruction from Sparse Views Generative priors have become a powerful remedy for sparse-view reconstruction. ReconFusion~ Wu2023ReconFusion3R regularizes NeRF optimization with image diffusion, while 3DGS-Enhancer~ Liu20243DGSEnhancerEU , Difix3D+~ wu2025difix3d+ , and GenFusion~ Wu2025GenFusionCT distill restored novel views into 3D representations. Video-based methods further improve temporal consistency through scene- or reference-grounded guidance~ Zhong2025TamingVD,yin2025gsfixer , long autoregressive generation~ de2026artifixer , or large-scale restoration training~ wang2026artifactworld . Although these methods refine the resulting 3D representation, their main advances center on the generator, leaving the initial reconstruction largely unchanged. Beyond static scenes, NeoVerse~ Yang2026NeoVerseE4 and One4D~ Mi2025One4DU4 extend coupled generation and reconstruction to dynamic 4D scenes from monocular videos or sparse frames. PanoWorld~ Jia2026PanoWorldAG similarly maintains a dynamic 3DGS cache, but relies on single-image diffusion to update it, making independently generated views susceptible to cross-view inconsistencies similar to those observed in DiFix. In contrast, we globally optimize a unified 3DGS from observed panoramas and use generation to densify missing evidence while preserving scene identity along continuous trajectories. Method Correspondence-Guided Geometric Optimization sec:holi_reconstruction Sparse panoramic inputs provide limited overlap and often contain large textureless regions, where conventional feature matching yields too few reliable constraints for 3DGS optimization. We therefore leverage a frozen feed-forward large reconstruction model (LRM) as an offline correspondence teacher. As shown in Appendix Tab.~ tab:matching_points , conventional feature-based matchers such as i3dgs~ 2026immediate3DGS and COLMAP~ pan2024glomap are insensitive to the number of input views because they operate pairwise, but produce too few reliable correspondences on sparsely textured indoor surfaces. LRMs provide substantially denser matches, although the number of forward--backward-consistent correspondences decreases when additional context views are jointly processed. We therefore select nearby view pairs with sufficient co-visibility and process each pair independently with DA3~ lin2025depth , yielding a dense set of reliable correspondence anchors for subsequent 3DGS optimization. Given a candidate pair , the LRM predicts dense geometry, relative camera transformation , and per-pixel confidence. For each source point , we obtain its target coordinate and forward--backward error as We retain only valid, confident correspondences satisfying and collect them as fixed anchors , where is determined by the LRM confidence and forward--backward error. These correspondences are computed once before training and held fixed during the initial 3DGS optimization. Similar to the multi-view geometric regularization used in GaussianPro~ Cheng2024GaussianPro3G and PGSR~ chen2024pgsr , we use them as fixed cross-view references for geometric supervision. Because the correspondences are not re-estimated from the evolving 3DGS, they help stabilize optimization in texture-poor regions. In-the-Wild Generative Prior Adaptation data construction. We construct a generative adaptation corpus from over 1K multi-room real-estate scenes. For each scene, we build a co-visibility graph over its panoramas and partition them into a connected reconstruction set and a held-out target set. We optimize a 3DGS using only the retained panoramas, following the same reconstruction pipeline and hyperparameters used at inference. All perspective views derived from held-out panoramas are excluded from this reconstruction. Renderings at held-out camera poses provide naturally degraded inputs, while the corresponding panoramic reprojections supply ground-truth RGB supervision. Reference views are selected from nearby retained panoramas. This construction preserves the natural artifacts caused by sparse coverage, texture-poor regions, and viewpoint extrapolation. The right panel visualizes the split and co-visibility graph; tiers A and B use strict and permissive coverage criteria, respectively. -image restoration. For each sparse ground-truth anchor view sampled from a held-out panorama, we pair its 3DGS rendering with the corresponding panoramic reprojection and obtain a reference view from a nearby retained panorama. DiFix additionally receives normalized rendered inverse depth through its confidence branch: consistent video restoration. As illustrated in Fig.~3 (left), we reproject each held-out panorama into perspective frames along a rotational trajectory with a fixed camera center. title: GS-PRM: Gaussian Visual Roadmap for Image-Goal Navigation
summary: Image-goal navigation requires a global planner that connects visually specified endpoints while providing observations that a local policy can follow. Three-dimensional Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides map-registered RGB, opacity, and depth renderings, but does not explicitly encode navigable topology. We introduce GS-PRM, a Gaussian visual roadmap whose milestones, local connections, and visual references are constructed directly through 3DGS rendering without deriving an occupancy grid or signed distance field. We define render-based collision-free (RC-free) configurations and paths. Panoramic depth supplies conservative clearance for milestone validation and adaptive coverage, while edge-aligned orthographic rendering tests the robot's swept volume. We establish conditional soundness and sufficient conditions for deterministic query completeness and probabilistic construction completeness of GS-PRM. To validate the performance of GS-PRM, we conduct experiments in both simulated and real-world environments, demonstrating long-horizon navigation using goal-conditioned policies guided by GS-PRM. Compared with a state-of-the-art 3DGS-based navigation system, our GS-PRM-based navigation system achieves up to a twice higher average success rate and reduces travel time by up to 57.2% when both systems complete the navigation task.

Introduction Image-goal navigation is a visual navigation problem that requires an agent to navigate to the location represented by a given goal image 9981090 . The image conveys appearance, but neither the goal pose nor a traversable route, and the destination is usually outside the current camera view. A goal-conditioned visual policy can reliably act only toward a nearby, recognizable observation within its training and control horizon. Long-horizon navigation, therefore, requires a persistent global topology that connects the localized query images and decomposes the route into reachable visual subgoals. It must also provide map-registered observations for repeated pose correction, since odometric drift can otherwise cause the physical robot to deviate from the planned route. This task requires two forms of persistent scene information: a global planner needs the connectivity of traversable space, whereas the online robot needs map-registered visual observations for localization and feedback. Probabilistic roadmaps (PRMs) construct a reusable graph by sampling collision-free milestones and connecting them through geometrically validated local paths~ kavraki1996probabilistic,lavalle2006planning . However, conventional PRMs assume sufficiently accurate workspace geometry for collision checking, which can require many expensive collision tests. For physical robots, reconstruction and localization errors can further invalidate these geometric tests. Moreover, conventional PRMs lack the visual observations needed for image-based localization and feedback. Three-dimensional Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is attractive in this setting because it represents metric, map-registered appearance and supports fast rendering of RGB, opacity, and depth from arbitrary viewpoints~ kwon2023renderable . These renderings can provide visual references for localization and geometric evidence for planning through a common scene representation. However, since raw Gaussian primitives are optimized for view synthesis and do not directly correspond to physical obstacles, a render-native planner must explicitly define what its renderer certifies. Existing Gaussian-map planners take several approaches to this problem. SplatNav performs collision checking against Gaussian confidence ellipsoids and constructs safe volumes~ chen2025splat . GaussNav and related systems derive voxel, bird's-eye-view, or other planning maps from a Gaussian scene~ lei2025gaussnav,chopra2025splatblox . Other work directly renders visual subgoals for a learned navigation policy~ honda2025gsplatvnm . These methods demonstrate that 3DGS is useful for navigation. Still, they do not provide a persistent coverage-induced roadmap in which the same rendering interface defines milestone validity, local connectivity, image queries, and visual route references. We address these limitations with , a coverage-driven Gaussian visual roadmap. PRM provides a persistent multi-query topology, while 3DGS provides map-registered observations that are absent from a conventional roadmap. Using a single rendering interface, evaluates milestones and local connections, attaches image-defined endpoints, and generates visual references along the selected route. We introduce the concept of render-based collision-free (RC-free), a conservative notion of free configuration space under some rendering assumptions, providing a relationship between rendered evidence and planning. Clearance-adaptive coverage then reduces redundant milestones in open areas while retaining finer resolution near constrained regions. The contributions of this work are: We construct a Gaussian visual roadmap from the same map-registered 3DGS renderings used for planning, localization, and image-goal guidance, without deriving a separate occupancy or distance-field planning map. We define RC-free milestones and local connections using conservative, thresholded depth, and state the assumptions under which their accepted configurations and paths lie within physical free space. We construct a connected roadmap from certified clearance-adaptive regions and establish sufficient conditions for probabilistic construction completeness and deterministic query completeness of a completed roadmap. For long-horizon visual navigation, we integrate image-based endpoint localization, validated roadmap attachment, and rendered visual subgoals for a goal-conditioned local policy. Related Work Probabilistic Roadmaps for Navigation The classical PRM separates an offline learning phase, in which sampled milestones and locally feasible connections approximate free-space connectivity, from an online query phase~ kavraki1996probabilistic . Uniform, obstacle-based, bridge, Gaussian, visibility, and deterministic sampling strategies trade construction cost against narrow-passage discovery and dispersion; an overview is provided by LaValle~ lavalle2006planning . PRM variants have subsequently been adapted to navigation. T-PRM predicts the temporal availability of roadmap vertices in the presence of moving obstacles~ HupChl22 . PRM-RL accepts edges by rolling out a learned short-range policy rather than relying solely on a straight-line local planner~ FauTap18 . These methods exploit metric relationships among configurations but normally assume a geometric or state representation on which collision checking is defined. instead defines roadmap validity and coverage through 3DGS rendering and associates the resulting roadmap with visual observations for online navigation. 3D Gaussian Splatting for Robot Navigation 3DGS combines an explicit set of spatial primitives with fast novel-view synthesis~ kerbl20233d . Gaussian Splatting SLAM demonstrates that a Gaussian scene can jointly support online mapping, camera tracking, and novel-view rendering, while GSplatLoc estimates camera pose by aligning observed and rendered depth~ matsuki2024gaussian,zeller2025gsplatloc . These works establish 3DGS as a map-registered visual representation, but do not supply the persistent traversability graph required for multi-query planning. Gaussian-map planners differ in how they obtain collision geometry. GaussNav constructs a semantic Gaussian map for image-goal matching and converts it to a grid for path planning~ lei2025gaussnav ; SplatBlox similarly derives a planning-oriented spatial representation~ chopra2025splatblox . SplatNav instead checks collisions against Gaussian confidence ellipsoids and constructs safe volumes~ chen2025splat . These methods either derive auxiliary planning geometry or reason directly about Gaussian primitives. Rendering has also been used as the interface to a visual policy. GSplatVNM synthesizes intermediate point-of-view images that bridge gaps in a sparse image database~ honda2025gsplatvnm , and 3DGSNav renders informative views from a persistent Gaussian memory for long-horizon object navigation~ zheng2026gsnav . In contrast, builds a reusable coverage roadmap whose milestone test, connection test, image-query interface, and visual route references are all defined through rendering. Rendered depth is not automatically a conservative collision oracle. It may be affected by missing surfaces, low accumulated opacity, depth blending, thin objects, finite raster resolution, and view dependence. We therefore make the relationship between rendered evidence and physical collision freedom an explicit assumption and evaluate it separately from roadmap connectivity. Goal-Conditioned Visual Navigation Image-goal policies infer short-horizon motion or waypoints from the current observation and a goal image. GNM learns this interface from heterogeneous robot datasets, and ViNT scales it into a reusable navigation model that generalizes across environments and embodiments~ shah2023gnm, shah2023vint . NoMaD further models multimodal action sequences using a goal-masked diffusion policy and supports both goal-reaching and exploration~ sridhar2024nomad . Related approaches combine learned local control with topological memory or high-level goal proposal for longer-horizon navigation~ hatch2025ghil,Yang-RSS-23 . These policies remain local and require a reachable, visually informative goal. supplies a render-validated global graph in which pose-indexed observations serve as subgoals and localization references, extending the policy horizon without requiring a densely recorded image graph. title: Back on Track: Deployment-time Policy Improvement via World Model Planning
summary: State-of-the-art visuomotor policies are increasingly capable of executing complex tasks, yet can fail during deployment in ways they cannot predict or recover from on their own. Improving their performance and robustness typically requires collecting more data, retraining, or modifying the policy architecture, all of which are time- and resource-intensive in practice. We instead propose an offline-trained monitoring-and-intervention framework that improves a policy during deployment using only black-box query access. From a limited set of labeled on-policy rollouts, we learn a policy-conditioned liveness value that measures the nominal policy's progress toward task completion; we additionally train a compact latent world model using these rollouts together with play data. At deployment, the liveness value continuously monitors execution. When it detects a loss of progress, a short-horizon planner searches the world model for corrective actions using the same value as its planning objective, after which control returns to the nominal policy. We evaluate our method on the LIBERO-Goal task suite and on a Franka Panda manipulator, using the vision-language-action model $π_{0.5}$ and a diffusion policy as nominal policies, and demonstrate significant improvements in task success rates, while supporting real-time control. Additional results and videos are available on the project website (https://policy-improvement-wm.pages.dev/).
